newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Hudson Timber up as Britomart hurdle passed.
newsitem.headline: Hudson Timber up as Britomart hurdle passed.

text.p: Shares in diversified group Hudson Timber & Hardware Ltd rose sharply in light trade on Thursday after the controversial Britomart project in New Zealand cleared another hurdle.

Hudson said the New Zealand Stock Exchange had approved the prospectus of Pacific Capital Assets Ltd, which plans to raise development funds for the 3.125 hectare high-rise project on the Auckland waterfront.

On completion of the issue, project backer and seed capital investor Hudson would hold 33.75 million NZ$1 ordinary shares partly paid to NZ$0.50 cents in Pacific Capital and 16.875 million fully paid second ranking shares.
"We're entitled to about NZ$33 million of shares in this company, so that will pretty well double shareholder's funds," Hudson chairman David Sutton told Reuters.
An initial public offering planned to raise about NZ$65 million, while the company already had about NZ$105 million of capital, Sutton said.

Britomart, which would be the largest property development in New Zealand in the next decade, had approval for 11 high rise buildings -- likely to made up of four apartments, two hotels and five office towers, he said.

The project ran into difficulties in May when the Auckland Regional Council refused consent for dewatering on the grounds it could cause subsidence, but the Auckland City Council has appealed to the Environment Court.
Sutton said it was hoped outstanding resource consents would be granted by September or October, allowing construction to proceed.
Hudson share ended 20 cents higher at A$1.40, it high for the year, with 51,500 shares changing hands.
